slot.brief: Given spin-only magnetic moment of a transition metal ion, back-calculate the number of unpaired electrons and identify the metal ion.

stem: A transition-metal ion has a spin-only magnetic moment of $\sqrt{15}\ \text{BM}$. Which ion can it be?

verdicts.working: For spin-only moment, μ = √[n(n+2)] BM. √15 BM gives n = 3 unpaired electrons. V²⁺ has configuration 3d³, with three unpaired electrons.

working:
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$; $15=n(n+2)\Rightarrow n=3$; $\text{V}^{2+}:[\text{Ar}]3d^3$.

Independent check: For spin-only moment, μ = √[n(n+2)] BM. √15 BM gives n = 3 unpaired electrons. V²⁺ has configuration 3d³, with three unpaired electrons.
solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\,\text{BM}$.
$$15=n(n+2)\Rightarrow n=3$$
$\text{V}^{2+}$ has configuration $[\text{Ar}]3d^3$, with three unpaired electrons.
